assessment: This paper reports a novel regulatory mechanism that modulates RIF1 function during the DNA replication stress response. The authors identify three residues within the mouse RIF protein that can be phosphorylated in an ATM/ATR-dependent manner. Interestingly, this phosphorylation is dispensable for the ability of RIF1 to limit double-strand break resection but is required to protect stalled replication forks. The results are of clear interest for the field of DNA replication and repair.
